description: Page margin exercised through an explicit 40px body margin (fixtures may not use @page); a filled, bordered content box is inset uniformly inside the single Letter page.

page-break-after:always on the LAST in-flow block (nothing follows) must NOT emit a trailing blank page — Chrome renders one page, not two. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (1) as well as page-1 content, which catches the trailing-blank-page bug the page-1-only comparison used to hide.
page-break-before:avoid on content that already fits on one page is a no-op; both blocks remain stacked. Tracks the legacy avoid-value gap.

Modern break-inside:avoid keeps a card intact on a single page. Content already fits, so the rendered result equals an unbroken nested box. The modern break-inside property is now parsed and honored (see break-inside-avoid-real for the cross-page case).

Modern break-before:page on the first block is a no-op (no preceding content): the forced break is suppressed at the document start, so a single page renders. The modern break-* family is now parsed and wired into the forced-break path (see break-before-page-modern-real for the real two-page case).

orphans:3/widows:3 on a paragraph whose lines all fit on one page have no visible effect; a single-page guard that the orphans/widows properties parse and never regress the no-break case (real cross-page fragmentation is covered by orphans-widows-default, orphans-3, widows-3, widows-4, orphans-4).

content: counter(page) used in NORMAL DOCUMENT FLOW (.pagenum::after) is an ordinary undefined counter that resolves to 0 in both Chrome and ironpress (the page/pages counters are special only inside @page margin boxes, which ironpress now supports — see the render_at_page_margin_box_counters_three_pages PDF-text test). This fixture locks in the in-flow 0-resolution parity with Chrome.
page-break-inside:avoid on a table that already fits keeps the whole table on one page. Tracks the legacy page-break-inside gap with a geometry-deterministic table.

The page property names an @page rule (page: cover) on the document's FIRST block, with no matching @page cover rule. Named pages are now parsed (CSS Paged Media 3 §3.4): the property forces a page break before the box, but a forced break at the very start of the fragmentation flow is suppressed, so a single page renders with the section on the default page — matching Chrome. The named-page MARGIN application is covered by paged-named-page-margin.

A background declared on @page paints the bleed area — the entire page box INCLUDING the @page margins (CSS Paged Media 3 §3.1). The 40px margin band is filled; a white bordered card sits inset in the content box.

A propagated :root/canvas background is the document canvas, confined to the page content box — it does NOT paint the @page margin band (CSS Paged Media 3 §3.1). Same geometry as at-page-background-bleed, but the 40px margins stay white; the blue fills only inside them.

page-break-before:always puts the second box on page 2, so the document is genuinely TWO pages. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs BOTH pages against Chrome (page 1 = blue box, page 2 = green box) — a real pagination test, not a single-page no-op.

Modern CSS Fragmentation break-before:page (no legacy fallback) on the second block forces it onto page 2 — a genuine TWO-page document. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages (page 1 = blue box, page 2 = green box). Proves the modern break-* family is now parsed and wired into the forced-break path.

Modern CSS Fragmentation break-after:page on the first block forces the following content onto page 2 — a genuine TWO-page document. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

break-inside:avoid keeps a bordered card together across a page boundary: a tall spacer fills most of page 1, so the card would straddle the boundary and is pushed WHOLE onto page 2 (not split). The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2): page 1 = spacer, page 2 = intact card.

A five-line paragraph taller than the @page content box (which fits four lines) is fragmented across two pages. With the initial orphans:2/widows:2, a naive greedy fill (4 lines on page 1, a single widow on page 2) is corrected so each fragment keeps >=2 lines: Chrome puts 3 lines on page 1 and 2 on page 2. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages — a real orphans/widows test, not a single-page no-op.

orphans:3 requires at least three line boxes at the bottom of a fragment before a break. The five-line paragraph fragments across two pages; the break leaves 3 lines on page 1 and 2 on page 2 (Chrome). The harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

widows:3 requires at least three line boxes at the top of the next fragment after a break. The five-line paragraph fragments across two pages; the break moves earlier so the continuation starts with 3 lines, leaving 2 on page 1 (Chrome). The harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

CSS Paged Media 3 §3.3: @page :first sets a 128px top margin on page 1 only; page 2 keeps the 32px default. The harness compares both pages on integral 300-DPI boundaries, isolating the :first cascade from fractional endpoint sampling.

widows:4 forces at least four line boxes onto the continuation page. An eight-line paragraph in a six-line page would naively split 6/2, but widows:4 moves the break two lines earlier to 4/4 (Chrome). The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

orphans:4 requires at least four line boxes left at the bottom of a fragment. A 100px spacer leaves only three line-slots on page 1, so the five-line paragraph cannot satisfy orphans:4 there and is pushed WHOLE to page 2 (Chrome); the initial orphans:2 would instead split it. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

Legacy page-break-inside:avoid on a TABLE that would straddle a page boundary: a 150px spacer leaves too little room for the 160px table. Chrome keeps the table whole and pushes it to page 2; ironpress now honors table-level keep-together too (the avoid-inside table fits a full page, so the whole row run is moved to page 2 instead of split between rows, matching the block-level keep-together in break-inside-avoid-real). The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

break-inside:avoid on a <figure> (image + caption) that would straddle a boundary: a 200px spacer leaves too little room, so Chrome keeps the figure together and pushes it WHOLE to page 2 (image and caption stay on the same page). The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

Modern break-after:page on the SECOND of three blocks forces the third block onto page 2 while the first two share page 1 — proving the modern break-after path fires mid-flow, not only on the first/last element. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

CSS Paged Media 3 §3.2 :left/:right spread margins: the right page has a 96px left margin and the left page a 96px right margin, while the opposite edges remain at the 32px default. The two-page assertion uses integral 300-DPI coordinates and isolates spread-selector geometry.

Legacy page-break-before:always on the THIRD of three blocks moves it to page 2 while the first two share page 1 — proving the legacy forced break fires mid-flow. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

Legacy page-break-inside:avoid on a bordered CARD that would straddle a boundary: a 220px spacer leaves too little room, so Chrome (and ironpress) push the whole card to page 2. Confirms the legacy alias is honored for block containers. The multi-page harness asserts the page COUNT (2) and diffs both pages.

CSS Paged Media 3 §3.4 named pages: page: wide on a .cover block forces a page break and the page it starts (page 2) adopts the @page wide margin (16px) instead of the default @page margin (32px). The multi-page harness asserts the page count and compares both page geometries on integral 300-DPI boundaries, avoiding a non-semantic fractional-raster edge.

CSS Paged Media 3 §3.4 named-page SIZE: @page big { size: A3 } selected by .big { page: big } makes page 2 physically A3-sized while page 1 keeps the default 400px by 304px size. The authenticated WeasyPrint reference uses the standard 297mm by 420mm A3 MediaBox; box edges use integral 300-DPI geometry so the assertion isolates per-page size selection.

CSS GCPM float: footnote pulls a box into the page's footnote area with an auto-numbered call marker left in the body text. The standards-derived source materializes GCPM relocation and its normative baseline-aligned font-variant-position:super call, without prescribing renderer-specific synthetic glyph metrics.

reference.note: CSS GCPM 3 section 2.6 defines the default footnote call as a superscripted counter with vertical-align:baseline, font-size:100%, line-height:inherit, and font-variant-position:super. Ironpress emits that superscript without moving the body line; WeasyPrint leaves the call full-size on the baseline, so its PDF is a compatibility canary, not a normative pixel oracle.

description: CSS GCPM running elements: position:running(runhead) removes a sized, painted box from normal flow and element(runhead) places that exact box in @top-center. The gold flow probe must start at the content top; this avoids text-metric noise and directly checks moved-box geometry. Validated against WeasyPrint because Chrome --print-to-pdf does not implement GCPM running elements.
A single table row taller than the page content box slices its cell background across page fragments.
A column-span: all heading inside a multi-column block interrupts the columns; column flow resumes and fragments across page boundaries.

reference.note: Ironpress and Chrome have the same two-page fragmentation, span-all interruption, paragraph assignment, and background geometry. The raw overlay contains text contours only: Chrome places the first text at 27.003661pt, while Ironpress 27.266009pt matches WeasyPrint's 27.266010pt for the common layout. CSS Multicol does not prescribe Chrome-specific baseline quantization. Raw shared-pdftoppm evidence remains reported.

description: break-after:right after a full first page must insert a blank left page so the next real block starts on a right page; catches implementations that alias right to an ordinary page break.

At a shared class-A break point, break-before:right on the following block must win over break-after:left on the preceding block; catches paginators that emit independent breaks and suppress the later side request.
@page :blank must style the blank page inserted by a sided break; catches implementations that insert the parity page but leave it with the default page rule.
Empty @left-middle and @right-middle generated boxes must paint their side-margin backgrounds; catches renderers that only implement top and bottom margin boxes or suppress empty boxes.

A block assigned page:chapter must use the chapter @page top-center margin box instead of the default one. Both generated boxes use a page-width color band and an invisible space, isolating named-page selection from page-margin auto-width behavior and text metrics.
A paginated table must repeat the thead and tfoot bands on each page fragment; integer-raster page geometry catches table splitting that fragments rows but forgets header/footer group repetition.
A vertical flex container taller than one page should continue its child items on later pages; catches paginators that treat flex containers as unsplittable atoms.

CSS GCPM footnote-policy:line keeps the line with its first footnote call on the following page while the preceding line remains on the current page; footnote-display:inline lays the note bodies inline. The verified standards-derived source materializes CSS Fonts 4's required synthesized superscript because ParitySans has no sups glyphs and Chromium does not synthesize the missing form.

string(section,last) and element(head,last) in page margin boxes must use the last heading on the page; catches GCPM implementations that ignore named strings or only support element(name)'s default selection.
break-after:left on page 2, a left page, must insert a blank right page so following content starts on page 4; catches implementations that alias left to an ordinary page break.
break-before:verso after two full pages must skip the natural right page and land on the next left page; catches parsers that treat verso as page or only recognize left/right.
break-before:recto on the first in-flow block must not create a leading blank page; catches implementations that insert parity pages before suppressing leading breaks.

At a shared class-A break point, break-before:left on the following block must override break-after:right on the preceding block; catches independent-break implementations that insert a blank page for the earlier value.
break-after:avoid keeps two adjacent solid boxes on the same page when they fit together; catches implementations that parse avoid but treat it as a no-op for automatic page breaks.
break-before:avoid-page keeps two adjacent solid boxes on the same page when they fit together; catches paginators that ignore break-before avoidance during automatic breaks.
break-before:page on a wrapper's first in-flow child propagates to before the wrapper; catches layouts that break inside the wrapper and leave wrapper decoration on the previous page.
break-after:page on a wrapper's last in-flow child propagates after the wrapper; catches layouts that fragment the wrapper decoration onto the following page.
break-inside:avoid-page keeps a page-fitting card intact when it would straddle a page boundary; catches parsers that support avoid but not avoid-page.
Rows in a one-column grid continue across page fragments instead of clipping as one atomic grid; catches paginators that lose lower grid rows while block/table fragmentation works.
A tall object-fit:fill image must show continued colored bands across later pages; catches renderers that treat replaced content as monolithic and clip it after page one.
A bordered tall replaced image must continue its image content and border decoration across pages; catches splitters that only handle undecorated images.
A tall element assigned page:chapter keeps the chapter page size and margin on continuation pages; catches named-page implementations that apply geometry only to the first fragment.
@page size:ledger selects the 11in by 17in page box; catches page-size parsers that fall back after supporting only common sizes.
@page size:jis-b4 landscape selects the named JIS B4 sheet and swaps axes; catches parsers missing the JIS keyword or orientation combination.
@page margin with three values resolves top, horizontal, and bottom margins; catches parsers that ignore this shorthand arity.
@page margin:10% creates a visible inset from the page box; catches page margin parsers that accept only absolute lengths.
@page page-orientation:rotate-left rotates the rendered page after layout; catches size-only implementations that leave portrait output upright.
@page marks:crop cross emits printer crop and registration marks around the page; catches renderers that implement only page size, margin, and background.
@page bleed with crop marks paints the page background into the bleed area; catches renderers that clip backgrounds to the trim page box.
A comma-separated @page selector list applies one margin rule to title and chapter named pages; catches selector classifiers that store the whole list as one page name.
Named page selectors combined with :left and :right apply spread-specific margins only to matching chapter pages; catches named-only matching that drops pseudo-page selectors.
The first page also matches :right, so declarations from @page :first and @page :right both apply; catches resolvers that pick only one pseudo-page rule.
On a blank page inserted by break-after:left, the fixed-width @page :blank top-center band overrides @page :right; isolates blank-page selector specificity from non-normative text-metric differences.
Default @top-left, @top-center, @top-right, and @bottom-center page margin boxes render literal strings; catches visual parity gaps that only cover PDF-text margin box assertions.
A top-center page margin box applies its own color, background, and font size; catches content-only margin box renderers with hard-coded text styling.
@top-left-corner occupies the page corner while @top-left starts at the content edge; catches simplified top-band renderers that overlap or drop corner margin boxes.

@page :first replaces the default top-center header on page one only; catches engines that collect margin boxes only from unselected @page rules. The WeasyPrint Paged CSS oracle is used because Chromium's print path places the same margin-box line at a different baseline than the Page 3 fixed-dimension and line-box rules.

Page-context font-family, font-size, and line-height inherit into margin boxes, while :first overrides the page context and the nested margin rule overrides that page text. Catches engines that resolve one document-wide margin-box text default before selecting each physical page.
@page counter-increment:page 2 changes counter(page) in margin boxes; catches renderers that substitute the physical one-based page index.
@page counter-reset:page 7 changes the origin of counter(page) in margin boxes; catches renderers that ignore page-context counter reset.
counter-reset:page 7 with counter-increment:page 2 resolves each page-local counter to 9; catches renderers that carry a reset between pages or omit an explicit increment after it.
counter-reset:pages in the page context must not alter counter(pages), which remains the total page count; catches over-eager page counter implementations.
position:running() referenced from @page :first appears in the first-page header only; catches running-element support that ignores selected page margin boxes.
position:running() referenced from a named @page chapter margin box appears only on chapter pages; catches named-page geometry support that discards named margin boxes.

A nested GCPM @page/@footnote rule plus ::footnote-call and ::footnote-marker custom content affects the footnote area, calls, and markers. The call explicitly resets GCPM's default font-variant-position and uses baseline alignment, isolating pseudo-element styling from user-agent-defined superscript metrics. Chromium lacks native float:footnote, so the authenticated standards-derived source materializes the required page-area result without importing WeasyPrint's incompatible transformed-text rasterization. The fixture uses integral 300-DPI page geometry to isolate generated-footnote styling.
counter-reset:footnote changes generated footnote call and marker numbers; the verified standards-derived source preserves CSS Fonts 4 baseline-aligned synthesized calls.
footnote-display:compact places fitting short footnotes inline in the footnote area; the standards-derived source preserves CSS Fonts 4 baseline-aligned synthesized calls.

reference.note: CSS GCPM requires both fitting compact footnotes to share one inline footnote-area line at the page-area bottom, which both PDFs do. Ironpress preserves a 76.5pt separation between the body and footnote baselines; WeasyPrint preserves the same separation but shifts both by 0.1157pt. Chromium rendering of the independent standards-derived source matches Ironpress within 0.0021pt. The remaining raw signal is renderer-specific text contour and baseline quantization, not compact-footnote placement, so the WeasyPrint PDF is not a unique pixel oracle.

description: @footnote max-height is constrained when a page has body content, but GCPM exempts a footnote-only last page. The standards-derived reference preserves the full final footnote body rather than WeasyPrint 69's clipped output.

reference.note: CSS GCPM limits the footnote area with max-height except on a page containing only footnotes, and footnote-policy:auto permits the body to move to a later page. Both PDFs keep the call on page 1, move the complete body to the footnote-only page 2, and preserve the same three-line wrapping and rule geometry. Every body line in the WeasyPrint PDF is uniformly 0.1157pt lower; horizontal word bounds differ by at most 0.028pt. That renderer-specific baseline and glyph quantization is not prescribed by GCPM, so the WeasyPrint PDF is not a unique pixel oracle; raw shared-pdftoppm evidence remains reported.

description: footnote-policy:block moves the whole owning paragraph with its footnote when the note cannot fit. The verified standards-derived reference isolates that visible page-break geometry from unsupported footnote pseudo-element typography.

A large plain-weight top-center header remains visible after synthetic-bold document text. Chromium lacks page-margin generated content, so the verified standards-derived Foundation reference materializes CSS Page 3's fixed top-margin geometry and document-before-margin-box paint order. Catches PDF font-carrier state leaking from document content into later page decorations.
element(head, first-except) suppresses the running element on the page where it first appears but allows it later; catches parsers that only support element(name).
string-set with attr() feeds string(section,start) in the page header; catches margin header renderers without named strings or attr() support.
